properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/21/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/21/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 985709
Permit API: 081-21880
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/21/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator concerning the discovery of fluid with elevated electrical conductivity (EC) in the north central area of Pad B. It rained heavily while I was traveling up the access road and it stopped before I reached Pad B. Along the access road, a sediment discharge into UNT 18 to Frozen Run was observed. Sediment-laden fluid was observed flowing from the access road, underneath a section of silt fence, overtop of a line of compost filter sock, and entering the stream. It was noted in inspection report number 3505502 from 2/13/23 that the potential for a sediment discharge continued to exist in this location due to stormwater from the access road overtopping a line of compost filter sock. The Department recommends adding additional compost filter sock to prevent additional sediment discharges into the stream. Violations remain outstanding for the sediment discharge into the UNT 18 to Frozen Run along the access road. These violations remain outstanding against the ESCGP.On Pad B, the pad was covered with puddles of stormwater due to the recent precipitation. In the northcentral area of the pad, an excavated section approximately 60 feet by 10 feet is present along the pad edge where the pad meets the north stormwater channel. The EC of the fluid in this area was between 17.18 mS/cm and greater than 19.99 mS/cm. A sump is installed in the pad surface to the south of the north stormwater channel. Fluid is present in the sump approximately 2 feet down and an EC reading could not be obtained at this depth. The fluid in the north stormwater channel in the north central area had an EC of 11.97 mS/cm. The fluid flowing out of the northeast end of the north stormwater channel and into the lined sump has an EC ranging between 16.14 mS/cm and 19.18 mS/cm. The fluid within the lined sump at the end of the channel had an EC of 18.05 mS/cm. It appears that all of the fluid flowing out of the stormwater channel at the surface is being collected by the lined sump. No fluid was observed surrounding the sump. EC readings of the soil surrounding the sump were all below 200 uS/cm. In the northwest area of the pad surface where the dancefloor had been located, the stormwater had an EC of approximately 1600 uS/cm or less. The EC of fluid in the stormwater channel at the northwest corner of the pad was approximately 1400 uS/cm. Northwest of the MASS the fluid on the pad surface had an EC of 2.48 mS/cm. In the northeast corner of the pad surface, the EC of the fluid was 5.26 mS/cm. The fluid east of the MASS had an EC of 2.39 mS/cm. The fluid within the secondary containment southeast of the MASS was approximately 8 mS/cm. Fluid near the southeast corner of the pad, where elevated EC fluid was found by the Department on 2/6/23, had an EC of 2.80 to 4.68 mS/cm. The Department recommends screening the entire pad surface for elevated electrical conductivity and vacuuming up any fluid found with elevated electrical conductivity.Violations noted for the fluid discovered in the northcentral area of the pad surface. Due to the unknown volume and origin of this fluid, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/28/2026
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8286872
Permit API: 081-21212
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/28/2026
Comments: On August 28, 2026, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response inspection at the Range Resources Laurel Hill Well Pad B. Range Resources Kirby Steck reported on August 27, 2026 at 2135, a gasket for a filter pod failed causing a release of reuse water outside of containment. The filter pod was associated with a WMGR123 onsite supporting the Bear Hollow Well Pad stimulation. Upon arriving onsite, Range Resources had initially estimated the spill to be 15 to 20 gallons. When the DEP arrived onsite, Range Resources contractor had begun excavating the area of the fill slope of the well pad impacted by the release. The area of excavation at the time of arrival was approximately 10 feet by 10 feet and about 18 inches deep. Soil conductivity of the impacted area ranged from 3,000 to 6,000 uS/cm. Range Resources contractor continued to excavate the area of impact during the inspection. The area of impact had increased to approximately 20 feet by 10 feet and approximately 3 feet in depth. At 3 feet depth, Range Resources was finding elevated soil conductivity levels of 6,000 uS/cm. Prior to the DEP leaving the site, Range Resources determined that they would proceed with remediating the spill through the Act 2 process due to the spill being larger than initially estimated.Violations of Chapter 78a.56(a), Clean Streams Law 402(b), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted due to the release of reuse water outside of secondary containment onto the well pad slope.

Comments: Site inspection conducted on May 9, 2024 regarding a complaint called into the Department of a brine leak. I used a soil Hanna Groline soil probe to screen for conductivity. All readings exceeded the meters range of 4.00 mS/cm. A small drip was observed coming from the brine tank valve set area. The Department recommends monitoring the equipment and repainting or replacing the equipment if needed. A 5x Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were detected. Please note, the chart recorder has not been changed in months. The well tag has the previous operators name and contact information listed on. The Department recommends updating the contact information.

Inspection Date: 10/16/2025
Comments: On October 16 2025, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Uschak 2 Well Pad and associated wells.The findings were as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be properly installed. The Department observed an Emergency Response Plan and a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan that appeared to have all required information. The access road appeared to be stabilized with gravel, with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The well site appeared to exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed.At the time of inspection, the well pad had 5 total wells, all of which appeared equipped for production. The well tag was present on the 1H well head at the time of this inspection. Upon inspection of the 1H well head, the Department observed fluid actively leaking from the well head. The fluid appeared to be leaking from the handwheel on the wellhead. Stained and saturated gravel was observed beneath the well head in an area about 1 foot in diameter. A conductivity reading was taken of the fluid from the source of the leak on the handwheel with a reading of 14.00mS. Conductivity readings were taken in the stained and saturated gravel below the wellhead with readings of 2.81mS, 2.30mS, 4.64mS, 5.25mS. These readings were elevated in comparison to the background reading of 0.20mS.Prior to leaving the site the Department spoke to operator representative Brad Campbell via phone call and informed him of the observed leak. Mr. Campbell stated they would assess and ensure the leak is fix/remediated.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Upon inspection of the additional production equipment onsite, the production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks. There were no visible leaks with the GPU, and it appeared not to be in secondary containment, however the well was drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a.OGI referral is being requested for further evaluation of the well head and the observed corrosion.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/22/2023 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Knox Township, Jefferson county. 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING - DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery.  Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/22/2023
Violation Code: 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING - DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.
Violation ID: 8152137
Permit API: 065-25959
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Knox Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/22/2023
Comments: Inspection was conducted as an ongoing gas migration investigation and follow up violation inspection. Aaron O'Hara and I met with Heather from diversified as well as Seth Walker from national fuel at 157 Pump Station Rd which is the location of the gas migration and a compressor station. Moody and Associates was also on site collecting samples. While at the compressor station, Aaron collected water samples from the water well where gas could be heard bubbling from. 100% methane was detected in the headspace of the water well. We then drove to the gas well and inspected the well. At the time of the inspection we were unable to place slam bars in the ground because of standing water. There were no pressure gauges on the well at the time of the inspection. Heather from diversified is going to arrange a date and time to collect pressures from the well. The well records were reviewed and copies were attached to this inspection. Currently the well is in violation and will remain in violation until corrective measures are taken.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a Follow-up Inspection (FUI) of the Seneca Resources - DCNR 007 Pad K Well Site located in Delmar Twp, Tioga Co. on 7/5/22 @1045 hours. The weather was 70 degrees, light rain, winds S @5mph. Seneca Company Man, Travis Deleon was present onsite.During the previous inspection (IR#3376280) dated 6/10/22, a damp area and puddle was observed below the hose connection to the Highland production tank. The puddle had a field measured conductivity of 11.02 mS/cm. Sample 4427-261 was collected from the standing fluid and submitted to the DEP laboratory in Harrisburg for analysis. The sample results show the presence of a pollutional substance. Barium was reported at 44.78 mg/L, strontium was reported at 166.9 mg/L, and chlorides were present at 3410.8 mg/L. As of today's inspection, a small piece of secondary containment was observed installed under the hose connection on the rear side of the Highland storage tank. The area under the secondary containment was observed damp with a small amount of standing fluid. A Groline soil conductivity meter was used to measure the field conductivity of the damp soils from 1.97mS/cm - 2.37 mS/cm. A comparison of the previous photo taken of the area during the inspection on 6/10/22, to the current state of the area, indicates no pad material was removed from the impacted area. I spoke with a Seneca representative onsite and he stated production would be dispatching someone to the site to remediate the area today. A vac truck arrived onsite and removed the remaining production fluids from the Highland tank and drained the secondary containment. I again spoke with an onsite well tender regarding the removal of impacted pad material. He spoke with Jim Westbrook and stated Gas Field Specialists had been dispatched to the site and would arrive this afternoon. I completed my inspection and departed the site at 1300 hours. Gas Field Specialist personnel located me while conducting an inspection at the nearby Pad D. I informed them of the area with elevated conductivity on Pad K, where they were headed, and we discussed removal of the impacted pad material. They requested I return to the site after they had removed the impacted material to screen the area with a soil conductivity meter. None of the GFS personnel or onsite Seneca representatives possessed a conductivity meter. The impacted pad material was removed with shovels and 5 gallon buckets and placed on temporary secondary containment. I screened the excavated area for soil conductivity and found readings of less than 800 uS/cm. The area was backfilled with clean material and the secondary containment was repositioned under the hose connection. Comments: I conducted an Incident Response inspection of Diversified Production, LLC's Pickup Unit 1 well site (API 063-31495) in Green Twp., Indiana Co. This conventional well was drilled in July 1996 off Alder Road in Commodore, PA in a forested area.Diversified reported a brine release from the Pickup Unit 1 well site on 8/5/2024. A nipple rotted through a 100-barrel brine tank and approximately 12.5 barrels (525 gallons) was released onto the ground. The impacted area was approximately 8'x15'. I called William Warfel on 8/5/2024. He stated the production tank was emptied and disconnected from the well. Diversified was going to start digging today and cover the affected area with plastic. Today (8/7/2024), I visited the site. The production equipment was disconnected from the well, and the contaminated soil was under plastic. Due to the spill being greater than 42-gallons, the Department is requesting remediation and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Violations are noted below.

Unconventional: No

Comments: This is a well located within 2500' of an active gas migration area. At the time of inspection, well was equipped to produce. The tubing valve was closed, but the 4 1/2" was tied in and the valve pinched open. The annulus was closed. The well integrity appeared good at surface and no leaks were detected. However, I picked up as high as 46% LEL in the ground outside of the wellhead, farthest from the tank and then 8% gas between the wellhead and tank. Due to this, there is a problem with the well integrity downhole and the well is in violation. The well was labeled and equipped with a check calve, separator, line heater, regulator, and chart (last changed on 9/13). There was also a 100 bbl fiberglass tank tied in. The compressor had been shut off on September 28th, as you can see on the Barton chart where there is a pressure increase.

Comments: On June 11 2024, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of the Fay-Penn 14 Well located in Springhill Township, Fayette County in response to IR 3639535 where violations were issued for a heavily corroded production tank/piping. Accompanying on todays inspection is Tyler Metzger (WQS DEP) At the time of this inspection the access road appeared stabilized but is still surrounded by a plethora of overhanging tree branches, the Department is again recommending the Operator continue to monitor the vegetation around the access road to ensure the well site remains accessible by vehicle. The well site is exhibited greater than 70% vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The well tag is attached to the wellhead and the well posting is on site with all required information listed on it. Both the wellhead and production tank have no observable fluid leaks or fluid discharges coming from it. It appears that the Operator spray-painted over the words 'Not In Use" that was seen on the production tank during IR 3749199. At that time, the Department requested the Operator submit an NOV response noting whether the production tank is or is not in use by 5/17/24 and if it was not in use remove it from the site by 5/24/24. The Department has yet to receive a response from the Operator in regards to this well site. It also appears that the corroded piping attached to the production tank has been replaced and other heavily rusted areas appear to be spray-painted. The Department is again requesting the following by COB 6/27/24: Clarification on whether this production tank is being used or not, if it is not in use it then it be removed from the well site, what was done to the production tank/piping between this inspection and IR 3749199, and if the production tank is in use, clarification on whether there is any intent to do more to the rusted areas to prevent further corrosion from occurring.Based on todays inspection, violations issued during IR 3639535 shall remain outstanding pending a NOV response from the Operator and additional violations may be forthcoming dependent upon the status of the production tank.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8276197
Permit API: 111-20223
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/27/2026
Comments: On May 27, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management Inc's Neilan 1 gas well site located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4106039, where violations were issued for broken and corroded piping and a release from broken and corroded piping.At the time of this inspection, site conditions appear to be unchanged from IR 4106039, and to date, a Notice of Violation Operator response has yet to be received.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the gas wellhead with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the gas wellhead. At the time of this inspection, the Department attempted to contact the Operator by calling the number posted on the well tag, however, the number was not in service, therefore violations are being issued at this time for failure to have updated and accurate information posted on the well posting.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a small production tank adjacent to the gas wellhead, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this tank. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site. The tank on the left was observed to be green and the tank on the right was observed to be a faded green color. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the green (left) production tank on site, however, the faded green (right) production tank was observed to have several corroded pipes connected to it. Towards the top of the faded green (right) production tank, the Department observed an area where severe corrosion caused piping to break off. This broken pipe was observed to be on the ground at the base of the production tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this broken pipe, from the other corroded pipes still connected to the production tank, or the production tank at the time of this inspection. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the area at the base of the faded green production tank under/adjacent to the corroded pipes. Although, these soil conductivity readings (0.0328 mS, 0.0899 mS, and 0.0244 mS) are not elevated, it does not visual appear that the release that previously occurred has yet to be remediated as vegetation in this area appears to be distressed and the gravel in this area is stained. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed production equipment connected to a meter box, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment or meter box. Inside the Meter Box, the Department observed production paper that was dated 10/27/2023. A pile of pipes was observed on the ground adjacent to the meter box and production equipment, the Department recommends any equipment not in use be removed from the well site. Violations are being issued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not in use from the gas well site. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from corroded and broken piping is to remain outstanding at this time and new violations are being issued at this time for inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site.

Comments: On April 15 2025, the Department conducted a routine partial inspection of the Kovalic 13 Well Site.Upon inspection, it appears that an erosion channel has formed in the area of previous excavation and backfill. The erosion channel appears to start just downslope of the well head, and travels the full length of the backfilled area. The Department observed sediment deposited in the vegetated area where the erosion channel terminated. The Department did not observe any E and S BMPs installed on/around the site. The Department recommends the operator promptly ensure the site is properly stabilized and install E and S BMPs to prevent further migration of sediment and to minimize the potential for further sedimentation tooccur.Prior to leaving the site the Department contacted operator representative Heather Empfield to inform her of the observations made by the Department.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to properly temporarily stabilize the site and failure to implement E and S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.Transmittal of this inspection is delayed due to an IT app error.
